title: Cybersecurity Architecture: Fundamentals of Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability
why: Clear whiteboard walk-through of the CIA triad, the vocabulary every security conversation with a client starts from.

title: Cybersecurity Architecture: Five Principles to Follow (and One to Avoid)
why: Explains defense in depth, least privilege, separation of duties and secure by design in one sitting.

title: The Ultimate Beginner's Guide to Threat Modeling
why: Adam Shostack's four-question method is the simplest way to start threat modelling a client system.

title: Threat Modeling Cheat Sheet
why: Practical steps, STRIDE and diagramming guidance you can apply directly in a design review.

title: Building Secure and Reliable Systems
why: Google's free book on designing systems for security and reliability, including least privilege and recovery.

title: Security Engineering, Third Edition (free chapters)
why: The classic reference on how real systems fail, with every chapter downloadable for free.

title: Reflections on Trusting Trust
why: Short classic that shows why you cannot fully trust code you did not build, the root of supply chain security.

title: Reflections on Trusting Trust - Computerphile
why: Plain-language explanation of Thompson's compiler backdoor to pair with the paper.

title: The Protection of Information in Computer Systems
why: Origin of the design principles still quoted today, such as least privilege, fail-safe defaults and complete mediation.

title: Cybersecurity Architecture: Who Are You? Identity and Access Management
why: Covers IAM end to end: authentication, authorization, SSO, MFA and privileged access.

title: What is Multi-Factor Authentication
why: Three-minute explanation of authentication factors and why MFA matters.

title: How NOT to Store Passwords! - Computerphile
why: Shows why plain text and fast hashes fail and why salted slow hashing is the norm.

title: Password Storage Cheat Sheet
why: Concrete guidance on Argon2id, bcrypt, salts and work factors when you must store credentials.

title: NIST SP 800-63B Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication and Authenticator Management
why: The authoritative US standard on passwords, MFA and assurance levels that regulated clients cite.

title: An Illustrated Guide to OAuth and OpenID Connect
why: The friendliest visual explanation of OAuth 2.0 and OIDC, what each is for and how the flows work.

title: OAuth 2 Simplified
why: Concise reference to OAuth 2.0 roles, grant types and PKCE by one of the spec's editors.

title: Public Key Cryptography - Computerphile
why: Short intuitive explanation of public and private keys before you meet certificates and TLS.

title: 7 Cryptography Concepts EVERY Developer Should Know
why: Fast tour of hashing, salting, HMAC, symmetric and asymmetric encryption, signatures and key exchange with code.

title: SSL, TLS, HTTP, HTTPS Explained
why: Animated basics of what TLS does for data in transit.

title: The Illustrated TLS 1.3 Connection: Every Byte Explained
why: Byte-by-byte annotated TLS 1.3 handshake for when you need to really understand or debug it.

title: What is Secrets Management?
why: Explains why API keys and passwords belong in a vault, not in code or config files.

title: Secrets Management Cheat Sheet
why: Checklist for storing, rotating and auditing secrets in pipelines and cloud deployments.

title: OWASP Top 10
why: The industry baseline list of web application risks that clients and auditors will reference.

title: Running an SQL Injection Attack - Computerphile
why: Watching an injection attack happen makes the idea of untrusted input stick, which carries straight over to prompt injection.

title: OWASP Juice Shop
why: Deliberately insecure web app to practise finding OWASP Top 10 flaws hands-on.

title: Web Security Academy
why: Free, high quality labs covering every major web vulnerability class with guided solutions.

title: The Web Application Hacker's Handbook, 2nd Edition
why: The classic deep reference on web app attacks; dated (2011) but the fundamentals still hold.

title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
why: The standard risk list for LLM apps, the checklist to walk through for any AI build.

title: Explained: The OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
why: Walks through the LLM Top 10 risks in plain terms before you read the full document.

title: What Is a Prompt Injection Attack?
why: Gentle introduction to direct and indirect prompt injection and why it is hard to fix.

title: Generative AI's Greatest Flaw - Computerphile
why: Explains indirect prompt injection with concrete examples of how agents get hijacked.

title: Prompt injection (series)
why: The best running collection of writing on prompt injection by the person who named it.

title: The lethal trifecta for AI agents: private data, untrusted content, and external communication
why: A simple test for when an agent design is dangerous, directly usable in client design reviews.

title: Understanding prompt injections: a frontier security challenge
why: A model provider's own explanation of prompt injection risk and the layered defences they use.

title: Mitigating prompt injections in browser use
why: Shows how a model provider measures and reduces prompt injection for agents that browse the web.

title: Many-shot jailbreaking
why: Readable research post on how long context windows open a new jailbreak technique and how it was mitigated.

title: LLM Prompt Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
why: Practical defensive patterns for LLM apps in the familiar OWASP cheat sheet format.

title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
why: The paper that defined indirect prompt injection with real attacks on deployed apps.

title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design (CaMeL)
why: Proposes a system-level design that limits what injected text can do, rather than hoping the model resists it.

title: Lakera Agent Breaker (successor to Gandalf)
why: Hands-on game where you try to trick AI agents, which teaches attacker thinking fast; gandalf.lakera.ai now redirects here.

title: AI Red Teaming 101 - Full Course (Episodes 1-10)
why: Free full course from Microsoft's AI Red Team on how to probe generative AI systems.

title: MITRE ATLAS
why: Knowledge base of real adversary tactics against AI systems, the AI counterpart to ATT&CK.

title: Security vs. Privacy
why: Clears up the difference between protecting data and using it lawfully, which clients often blur.

title: What are the 7 principles of GDPR?
why: Short walk through the GDPR principles that shape any design using personal data.

title: Principle (c): Data minimisation
why: Regulator guidance on collecting only what you need, a key rule when feeding client data to AI.

title: Anonymisation guidance
why: Explains when data is truly anonymous versus pseudonymised and still personal data under GDPR.

title: The HIPAA Privacy Rule
why: Five-minute overview of what HIPAA protects and who it applies to.

title: HIPAA Explained
why: Readable overview of the Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules for US health data clients.

title: SP 800-218, Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1
why: The reference set of secure development practices that US government and regulated buyers expect.

title: SLSA: Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts
why: Framework for proving how build artifacts were produced, the practical side of supply chain security.

title: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
why: Explains SBOMs, which clients increasingly require so they know what components ship in your software.

title: Logging Cheat Sheet
why: What to log, what never to log, and how to protect logs so they work as an audit trail.

title: Part 11, Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures - Scope and Application
why: FDA guidance on how Part 11 applies to electronic records, audit trails and signatures in pharma and MedTech.

title: Computer Software Assurance for Production and Quality Management System Software
why: FDA's risk-based approach to validating software used in production and quality systems.

title: AI Risk Management Framework
why: The US reference framework for governing and managing AI risk, often cited by regulated clients.

title: Mastering AI Risk: NIST's Risk Management Framework Explained
why: Short explainer of the Govern, Map, Measure and Manage functions before reading the framework.

title: NIST AI 600-1: Generative AI Profile
why: Applies the AI RMF to generative AI with specific risks and suggested actions.

title: High-level summary of the AI Act
source: EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Future of Life Institute)
why: Readable summary of risk categories and obligations under the EU AI Act.

title: Google Cybersecurity Professional Certificate
length: under 6 months at 10 hours a week
why: Structured beginner program covering security frameworks, networks, Linux, SQL and incident response.

title: Introduction to security, compliance, and identity concepts
why: Short free path on core security, compliance and identity concepts, the base of SC-900.
